comment: Keeper arc 7 (canon section 7): The Hour Before (Tace). A new frost finds the loft window and Tace stops working. Umber, Mott, and Sorrel each hold one piece: the first hard frost was Wend's last night; Wend's tall ladder was put away at Tace's asking; Wend's climbing song, and a lamp in the loft window until the hour before midnight. Bringing the ladder home lets Tace take one small step toward the highest shelf. Endings: within-reach (the song: Tace climbs and sets the jar down where the lantern reaches, unopened), past-eleven (the stopped clock: Tace winds it past eleven and leaves it ticking under the shelf), another-season (timed: Tace goes as far as the bottom step alone, and takes the little stopped clock home to the loft shelf from whoever was keeping it). Never the full reveal: the jar stays sealed for a future dream.

things.name: round window
things.seed: old glass, faintly rippled, in a round frame worn smooth by elbows

state_text.clear: Through it the rooftops lean together like old friends.
state_text.frosted: Frost has grown across the glass in fine white lace, and in the middle someone has drawn a small clock face with one fingertip, both hands pointing at eleven.
state_text.thawed: The frost has gone, but a faint round mark stays on the glass where a clock face was drawn, like a breath that hasn't quite faded.

things.name: little brass clock
things.seed: a little brass clock no bigger than a pocket watch; on its back, scratched small in an old looping hand, is a single letter: W

state_text.stopped: It sits apart from the others on the top shelf, its hands standing at eleven; it hasn't ticked since the first hard frost.
state_text.kept: Its hands stand at eleven, and it hasn't ticked since the first hard frost.
state_text.ticking: It ticks now, soft and sure, on the bottom rung of Wend's ladder, its hands long past eleven.

do.text: You reach for the little clock. 'Not that one, friend,' Tace says quietly, without looking up.
It sits apart from the others as if it would rather not be moved. You leave it be.
It is ticking where Tace set it, under the highest shelf. You leave it there.
It sits back on the top shelf where Tace put it, hands at eleven. You leave it be, for another season.
It is already ticking, soft and sure, and doesn't need your hands. It seems glad of that.
You reach for the little key. 'Not that one, friend,' Tace says quietly.
The little key won't turn for you. Whatever this clock is waiting for, it isn't your hands.
Tace looks at the little clock, then at the stairs, and doesn't take it. 'You've cellar dust on your sleeve,' they say. 'What's standing down there, friend?'
Tace closes your fingers gently back over the little clock. 'Keep it a while longer, friend.'

things.name: tall ladder
things.seed: Wend's tall oak library ladder, its rungs worn pale in the middle by years of careful feet; like most dream things, it folds far smaller than it should

state_text.folded: Folded, it tucks under one arm.
state_text.standing: It stands against the highest shelf of the Hour Cellar now, reaching, just.

do.text: It already stands against the highest shelf, reaching, just.

do.text: You unfold Wend's ladder and lean it against the highest shelf. Umber nods at it, once. 'Wend's ladder. Standing. For another season.'
Umber shakes her head without looking up. 'Ladder: standing. Do not move.'
You leave it standing. It has waited long enough.
Not there. The ladder wants the highest shelf.
There's nothing here that needs a ladder so tall. It wants the Hour Cellar, and the highest shelf.

things.name: climbing song
things.seed: a few bars of Wend's old climbing song, folded small as a pressed leaf; held close, it hums, slow and a little off-key, and your feet feel surer for it

do.text: Tace hears the song humming in your hands and goes still. 'You've cellar dust on your sleeve,' they say. 'What's standing down there, friend?'
Tace hums a bar of it, and the tune climbs on without them. 'Wend's ladder song. It's had its singing for this season, friend.' They fold it back into your hands.
Tace listens to the folded song a moment and smiles, small and tired. 'Wend's ladder song,' they say. 'There's no ladder down there tall enough for it anymore.' They fold it back into your hands.

things.name: dusty jar
things.seed: a small jar set apart from all the others, its glass furred with dust except where Tace's thumbs have been, resting on the lowest shelf where the lantern reaches; a folded paper hour sits inside, and its label, in an old looping hand, is turned to face the wall; Tace set it down that way. The lid is still sealed

do.text: Your hand stops short of it. Tace set it just so, label to the wall, and it isn't yours to move.
The lid is sealed, and it isn't yours to open. Some jars wait for one pair of hands.

tace-hour.title: The Hour Before
tace-hour.summary: A new frost finds the loft window, and Tace stops working. Umber, Mott, and Sorrel each hold a piece of the night the great clock stopped, which was the night Wend died. Bringing Wend's ladder home to the Hour Cellar lets Tace take one small step toward the highest shelf, never the whole way.

tace-frost.hint: the player asks Tace about the frost on the loft window
tace-frost.text: Tace's hands go still, and stay still. They set a little brass clock in your palm, its hands at eleven. 'Keep this one for me a while, friend. Umber keeps a lamp lit on frost mornings.'

do.text: {actor} is keeping Tace's little stopped clock for them a while.

umber-frost.hint: the player asks Umber about the first hard frost, or about Wend
umber-frost.text: Umber sets down her pen, and for once doesn't mention tea. 'First hard frost. Wend's last night. Tace sat up; I took the tea at eleven.' Her eyes go to the dark above the lantern. 'Wend's ladder reached up there, once. Mott carried it off.'

mott-ladder.hint: the player asks Mott about Wend's tall ladder
mott-ladder.text: Mott sets the broom against the bench. 'Morning after the frost, Tace asked me to put Wend's ladder where they wouldn't have to see it.' He draws it out from behind a drift of shavings, folds it small the way dream things fold, and tucks it under your arm. 'Wend never climbed it without singing. Ask Sorrel for Wend's climbing song.'

do.text: {actor} is carrying Wend's old ladder back toward the Hour Cellar.

sorrel-song.hint: the player asks Sorrel about the song Wend sang going up the ladder, or about the night of the first hard frost
sorrel-song.text: Sorrel squints at the weather. 'First hard frost, a lamp burned in the loft window until the hour before midnight. Then the clock went quiet, and the frost came down like a held breath.' They hum a few slow, climbing bars and fold the tune into your hands. 'Wend's ladder song. It wants singing again.'

do.text: {actor} learned Wend's old climbing song from Sorrel.

ladder-set.hint: the player leans Wend's ladder against the highest shelf in the Hour Cellar

tace-told.hint: the player tells Tace that Wend's ladder is standing in the Hour Cellar again
tace-told.text: Tace looks down at the floorboards, as if they could see through them to the cellar. 'Standing again,' they say, very quietly. 'I'd go down, I think, if I had something to carry.'

within-reach.summary: given Wend's climbing song, Tace climbs the ladder and sets the jar from the highest shelf down where the lantern reaches, unopened
within-reach.text: Tace hums the folded song, low and a little off-key, all the way down to the Hour Cellar. Rung by rung they climb Wend's ladder into the shadow and come down with a small dusty jar, which they set, unopened, on the lowest shelf, label to the wall. 'Not yet,' Tace says. 'But I'd like to see it from the stairs.'
within-reach.ledger: {helpers} brought Wend's ladder home to the Hour Cellar and gave Tace the old climbing song; Tace climbed it, humming, and set a jar down where the lantern reaches.

do.value: the highest shelf, lost in shadow above the lantern's reach, with Wend's tall ladder leaning against it; where a single jar stood apart, there is only a clean circle in the dust
Tace looks up from a bench of small clocks, a smudge of cellar dust still on one sleeve, and offers a small, steady nod.

do.text: {actor} gave Tace Wend's climbing song, and Tace climbed the ladder humming it and brought a jar down to where the lantern reaches.

past-eleven.summary: given back the stopped clock, Tace winds it past eleven and leaves it ticking on the bottom rung of Wend's ladder, and does not climb this season
past-eleven.text: Tace finds the little clock's key and turns it, once, twice. It hesitates, then ticks, and its hands move past eleven for the first time since the frost. Down in the Hour Cellar, Tace sets it on the bottom rung of Wend's ladder and sits beside it with you a while, listening. 'Not the ladder. Not this season. But it's going again.'
past-eleven.ledger: {helpers} kept Tace's stopped clock a while; Tace wound it past eleven and left it ticking at the foot of Wend's ladder.

do.value: Tace looks up from a bench of small clocks, sets down a fine brass tool, and offers a tired, kind nod.

do.text: {actor} kept Tace's stopped clock until Tace was ready to wind it past eleven.

another-season.summary: unhelped for a week of frosts, Tace goes down the cellar stair alone as far as the bottom step, and Umber leaves tea there for next time
another-season.text: Frost comes and goes on the loft window all week. One night, very late, Tace goes down the cellar stair alone as far as the bottom step, looks up into the dark, and climbs back to bed. By morning the little brass clock is home on the top shelf, and Umber has left a cup of tea on the bottom step, for next time.
another-season.ledger: This season Tace went as far as the bottom step of the cellar stair, alone, and Umber left a cup of tea there for next time.

do.value: Tace looks up from a bench of small clocks, sets down a fine brass tool, and offers a tired, kind nod.

tace-hour-frost-window.text: A new frost has come to the loft window, and Tace has been standing at it instead of working. Frost mornings are hard on Tace.

tace-hour-wends-night.text: The first hard frost, the night the great clock stopped, was also the night Wend died. Tace sat up with Wend in the loft through the last of it, and Umber took the tea up at eleven.

tace-hour-ladder.text: Wend's tall ladder, the only one that ever reached the Hour Cellar's highest shelf, was put away in the Old Workshop at Tace's asking, the morning after the first hard frost.

tace-hour-song.text: Wend always sang the same slow climbing song going up the tall ladder. Sorrel still knows it.

tace-hour-jar-down.text: A jar that stood alone on the Hour Cellar's highest shelf now sits unopened on the lowest shelf, where the lantern reaches, its label turned to the wall. Nobody asks Tace about it.

tace-hour-clock-going.text: Tace's little clock, stopped at eleven since the first hard frost, is ticking again on the bottom rung of Wend's ladder in the Hour Cellar.

tace-hour-bottom-step.text: One night this season Tace went down the cellar stair alone, as far as the bottom step, and came back up. Umber left a cup of tea on the step for next time.

storylets.summary: a new frost finds the loft window, and Tace does not pick up a tool
storylets.text: The season's first frost comes in the night, thin as lace across the loft's round window. In the grey morning Tace stands at the glass with both hands in their apron pockets, and does not pick up a single tool.

do.value: Tace stands at the frosted window with both hands in their apron pockets, and the bench behind them sits untouched.

storylets.summary: Umber turns the lantern toward the jar on the lowest shelf
storylets.text: Before she settles for the night, Umber turns the lantern a little, so that its light falls on the dusty jar on the lowest shelf. Then she goes back to her labels.

storylets.summary: the little clock ticks on at the foot of Wend's ladder
storylets.text: At the foot of Wend's ladder the little clock ticks on, soft and sure. Umber has started setting her own slow pace by it.
